newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, no changes in sight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, no changes in sight.

text.p: Croatian stocks traded mixed on Thursday with marginal price fluctuations and analysts said no major changes were likely to shake the market before the end of the month.
"The companies should soon publish their annual business results and everybody is waiting for that," said Davor Relja, analyst at Faktor brokerage.
He said unofficial results should be known by the end of March, although no official information will be available before late April.
"I expect the current stagnation -- with some minor gains or losses -- to last until then," Relja said.
Four of fourteen active issues rose on Thursday, four fell and six were flat. Volume was somewhat higher at 9,487 units with turnover unchanged at 4.9 million kuna.
Drugs firm Pliva accounted for most of the day's trading, inching up eight kuna to 465 on volume of 6,655 shares.
Relja said renewed interest for Pliva was due to its higher price in London where its GDRs fetched $15.75 on Thursday.
Another fully-listed issue, Zagrebacka Banka, inched down five kuna to 1,730, with 632 shares sold. Its GDRs traded higher at $30.35 on Seaq International.
Zagrebacka's E-series preference stock added 17 kuna to 1,050, with 76 units traded.
Biggest gainer chocolate maker Kras rose 20 kuna to 520 on volume of 403 shares.
Biggest decliner insurer Croatia Osiguranje lost 100 kuna to 1,400 on volume of 25 shares.
Riviera closed at 1,800 kuna, Jadranturist at 300 and Laguna at 1,400. The only gainer was Istraturist which rose five kuna to 210.
Zagreb's hotel stock Intercontinental also remained unchanged at 170 kuna.
